name: City Council Meeting
minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  July 5, 2011

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, Housing Authority, and the Library Board of Trustees of the
City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Leckness at 5:01 p.m., on July 5,
2011, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on July 1, 2011, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Reardon
  Council Member Schlicht (arrived at 5:08 p.m.)
  Mayor Pro Tem Ury
  Mayor Leckness

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Irwin Bornstein, Former Asst. City Manager/Director of Admin. Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Reardon

INVOCATION: Mayor Leckness

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Real Property Negotiator pursuant to Government Code Section
  54956.8. Property is an approximate 10.5 acre Site commonly referred to as the
  “Former K Mart” located at 28601 Los Alisos Boulevard and Comprised of Assessor
  Parcel Nos. (APNs) 839-161-08 and 839-161-09 owned by Union Dominion
City Council Minutes  1  July 5, 2011
   Realty/Pacific Los Alisos L.P. (“UDR”). CDA negotiators: Dennis Wilberg, City
  Manager/CDA Executive Director, Charles Wilson, Director of Community
  Development, James Williams, Economic Advisor, Celeste Brady, CDA Counsel,
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney. Owner’s negotiators: Jeremy Cyr of UDR and
  John Ramirez, Kerra Carlson of Rutan & Tucker, Frank Spevacek of Rosenow
  Spevacek Group, ad Peter Whittingham of Curt Pringle Associates, all on behalf of
  UDR. Under negotiation: potential acquisition and/or disposition of real property
  interests for long term affordable housing and the price and terms of payment
  therefore related to the above-listed property. Factors affecting price and terms
  under negotiation: recorded covenants, scope of development of property, affordable
  housing requirements. Factors affecting time of payment: conditions to closing, due
  diligence period, and schedule of development and development of affordable
  housing.

CS2. Conference with Real Property Negotiator pursuant to Government Code Section
  54956.8. Property is an approximate 4.9 acre parcel near the northeast corner of
  Crown Valley Parkway and the I-5 freeway, with a common street address of 27741
  Crown Valley Parkway, Mission Viejo, CA 92691, identified as APN 761-111-16, and
  commonly known as Kaleidoscope (“Project”). The Project is currently owned by
  Crown Valley Holdings LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (“Owner” or
  “Developer”). The City of Mission Viejo (“City”) and Community Development
  Agency of the City of Mission Viejo (“CDA”) negotiators are: Dennis Wilberg, City
  Manager/Executive Director, Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of
  Public Services, Celeste Brady, CDA special counsel, and William P. Curley III, City
  Attorney. The Owner’s negotiators are: Colby Durnin of Sentinel Development
  Services, Inc. on behalf of Crown Valley Holdings LLC and counsel Timothy
  Carlyle. Under negotiation is the price or terms relating to the proposed amendment
  of that certain Agreement Affecting Real Property (“Covenants Agreement”)
  recorded against the Development Parcel and Project on July 8, 1999 of which
  covenants the CDA holds the beneficial interest and of which the City is an intended
  beneficiary. Factors affecting such price or terms: approval of an exception to a
  prohibited use, modification of maintenance and operational covenants, and other
  amendments to such Covenants Agreement, which have arisen from Developer’s
  request for the CDA’s consent to tenancy at the Project by LA Fitness.

CS3. Conference with the City’s Real Property Negotiators Pursuant to Government Code
  Section 54956.8. Real property Denoted as Assessor’s Parcel No. 784-291-01 with a
  Common Street Address of 24701 San Doval, Mission Viejo, California, Commonly
  Known as O’Neill Elementary School Owned by Saddleback Valley Unified School
  District. The Negotiating Parties are: City of Mission Viejo; Dennis Wilberg, City
  Manager, Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager, Charles Wilson, Director of
  Community Development, and William Curley, III, City Attorney. Owner
  Negotiators are: Saddleback Valley Unified School District, Clint Harwick,
  Superintendent. Under Negotiation will be the Price and Terms of a Lease-Hold
  Interest in the Real Property.

City Council Minutes  2  July 5, 2011
 CS4. Public Employee Performance Evaluation of the Incumbent for the Position of City
  Manager Pursuant to Government Code Sections 54957 and 54957.6.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:03 p.m., Mayor Leckness recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:04 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council received several updates and provided
direction to staff but there was no reportable action from Closed Session.

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Adoptable Pets of the Month

  Mayor Leckness announced that the Mission Viejo Animal Services Center will hold a
  “Puppy Party” adoption event on Saturday, July 9, 2011.

P2. Recognize Assistant City Manager and Director of Administrative Services Irwin
  Bornstein on his Retirement from the City

  Mayor Leckness presented a Certificate of Commendation to Irwin Bornstein.

*Items P3 and P4 were taken out of order.

P4. Target Symphony in the Cities "Prelude in the Park" Presentation

  Community Services Specialist Kathi Dickey announced that the Target Symphony in the
  Cities concert will be held on Saturday, July 30, 2011. Family activities begin at
  4:00 p.m. and this year’s theme is "Home Town Block Party." The concert, with Musical
  Director Carl St. Clair, will begin at 7:00 p.m.

P3. Proclaim July 2011 as National Recreation and Parks Month

  Mayor Leckness presented the proclamation.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Larry Gilbert, M.V.: stated that the Governor’s efforts to pass a budget have an impact on the
City’s redevelopment agency and he suggested that Special Counsel Celeste Brady provide the
Council with an overview of the issues and important dates.

Joe Alanes, M.V.: invited the Council and residents to the Modjeska Playhouse 2nd Annual
Summer Theater in the Park Production. "All the Great Books Abridged" will be presented on
City Council Minutes  3  July 5, 2011
 July 16 and 17, 2011, at 6:00 p.m. in the Kershaw Garden.

Drew Parsons, M.V.: thanked the City Council for a warm reception to his new business, The
Meat House, and he provided a brief description of the store and its services.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 4, 6, 8, 9, 11, 13, 14, 15, 17, 18 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate
discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further
  reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  (1) Approved the Minutes for the Budget Workshop of June 15, 2011, as presented; and (2)
  approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of June 20, 2011, as amended
  (page 4, film screening of John Adams was incorrectly listed as July 26. The date will be
  changed to June 26, 2011.)

3.  Check Register dated June 10, 2011 in the amount of $395,770.37

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Destruction of Records -- Citywide 2010 Records Purge

  Adopted Resolution 11-41A Authorizing and Directing the City Clerk to Destroy Certain
  City Records and Documents Pursuant to the Government Code of the State of California.

7.  Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA) Master Funding Agreement

  (1) Approved the Master Funding Agreement with Orange County Transportation
  Authority (OCTA) subject to any minor modifications required by the City Attorney and
  City Engineer; and (2) authorized the Mayor to sign the agreement on behalf of the City.
City Council Minutes  4  July 5, 2011
 10. Maintenance of Traffic Signals and Appurtenance, Interconnect, Flashing Beacons,
  Illuminated Street Name Signs, Safety Lights and CCTV Cameras-Contract
  Extension

  Approved the Fifth Amendment to Contract A07-48 with Republic ITS (A-7-48E)
  extending the term of the contract to September 30, 2011.

12. 2011 Residential Resurfacing (CIP 838)-Slurry Seal

  Approved the bid specifications and authorized staff to advertise for construction bids for
  the 2011 Residential Slurry Seal Project.

16. 2011-2013 School Crossing Guard Services

  (1) Awarded the contract in the amount of $731,000 to All City Management Services, Inc.
  (A11-53), for school crossing guard services for the period July 1, 2011, to June 30, 2013;
  (2) authorized issuance of a purchase order to All City Management Services, Inc., in an
  amount not to exceed $365,500 for the period July 1, 2011, to June 30, 2012, pending
  adoption of the 2011-13 Budget by the City Council; and (3) authorized the relocation of
  the crossing guard location for Bathgate Elementary School from the intersection of
  Barbadanes and Ridgemark to the intersection of Napoli and Ridgemark as recommended
  by the Planning & Transportation Commission at its May 9, 2011, meeting.

19. Purchase of Additional Disk Space for the Backup System

  Approved a purchase order to GovPlace for the purchase of additional disk space for the
  Data Domain backup system in an amount not to exceed $60,466.14.

20. Mileage Reimbursement

  Adopted Resolution 11-43 Adopting the Standard IRS Mileage Reimbursement Rate of
  55.5 Cents Per Mile for the Period From July 6, 2011 to December 31, 2011.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

28. Adoption of the 2011-13 Budget

  City Manager Wilberg presented the staff report.

  The following expressed concerns with the proposed budget: Matt Corrigan, M.V. and
  Harry Lenczyk, M.V.

City Council Minutes  5  July 5, 2011
   The following spoke in support of the proposed budget: Dan Avery, M.V.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to (1) adopt
  Resolution 11-45 Adopting a Budget for the City of Mission Viejo for 2011-13 and
  Appropriating Funds for FY 2011-12 Only; and (2) adopt Resolution 11-46 Establishing an
  Appropriations Limit for FY 2011-12; and (3) adopt Resolution 11-47 Updating the City’s
  Classification System and Establishing Salary Ranges for Authorized Job Classifications

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

29. Adoption of the 2011-13 Budget for the Mission Viejo Community Development
  Agency

  Former Assistant City Manager/Director of Administrative Services Irwin Bornstein
  presented the staff report.

  Larry Gilbert, M.V.: stated that there is a discrepancy with the proposed tax increment
  listed in the staff report for this item and the agenda report from a prior Council meeting.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to adopt CDA
  Resolution 11-10 Adopting a Budget for the Mission Viejo Community Development
  Agency for 2011-13 and Appropriating Funds for FY 2011-12 Only.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

30. Adoption of FY 2011-12 Budget for the Mission Viejo Community Development
  Financing Authority

  Former Assistant City Manager/Director of Administrative Services Irwin Bornstein
  presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to adopt
  CDFA Resolution 11-01 Adopting a Budget for the Mission Viejo Community
  Development Financing Authority for the 2011-12 Fiscal Year.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht and Ury
City Council Minutes  6  July 5, 2011
   NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

31. Adoption of FY 2011-12 Budget for the Mission Viejo Housing Authority

  Former Assistant City Manager/Director of Administrative Services Irwin Bornstein
  presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to adopt
  Housing Authority Resolution 11-04 Adopting a Budget for the Mission Viejo Housing
  Authority for FY 2011-12.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

OLD BUSINESS

21. Extension of the Rental Use Agreement with Outta Bounds Events for use of the
  Thomas R. Potocki Center for Youth Activities from September 6, 2011 through June
  30, 2012.

  Director of Recreation and Community Services Kelly Doyle presented the staff report.

  The following spoke in support of the extension of the rental agreement with Outta Bounds:
  Linda and Chris Orem, M.V.; Stephanie Christus, M.V.; Anita Armstrong, M.V.; Julia
  Oien, M.V.; Lindsay and Lexie Dutch, M.V.; Sally Mares, M.V.; Scott Ramirez, M.V.; and
  Nancy and Emily Enriquez, M.V.

  The following spoke in support of Modjeska Playhouse and/or in support of returning the
  matter to the Community Services Commission: Joyce Saltzgiver, M.V.; Chris Sullivan,
  Rancho Santa Margarita; Helen Workun, M.V.; and Dan Avery, M.V.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, to (1) approve
  an extension of the Rental Use Agreement between the City and Outta Bounds Events for
  use of the Thomas R. Potocki Center for Youth Activities through the summer of 2011; and
  (2) direct that City staff and Outta Bounds meet with the Capistrano Unified School District
  to inquire about relocating their program to the Newhart campus; and (3) direct the
  Community Services Commission to continue evaluating the other proposals that were
  submitted for the Thomas R. Potocki Center.

  On roll call, said motion failed by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley and Ury
City Council Minutes  7  July 5, 2011
   NOES:  Leckness, Reardon, and Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

  Motion made by Mayor Leckness, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve an
  extension of the Rental Use Agreement between the City and Outta Bounds Events for use
  of the Thomas R. Potocki Center for Youth Activities from September 6, 2011, through
  June 30, 2012, in the amount of $3,000 and actively work with Outta Bounds to seek
  another location for the program.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Schlicht
  NOES:  Ury
  ABSENT:  None

22. Annual Routine Street Sweeping Services

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  The following spoke in support of Sunset Property Services: Andrea Howhannesian, M.V.;
  Sherri Butterfield, M.V.; Tracey Gould, Sunset Property Services; John Howhannesian,
  Sunset Property Services, M.V.; Steve Greyshock, South Orange County Chamber of
  Commerce; Mike Conte, M.V.; Ron James, M.V.; Nina Altountash, M.V.

  The following spoke in support of the staff recommendation to award a contract to Athens
  Services: Larry Gilbert, M.V.; Brett R. Barbre, Athens Services; and Joe Homs, M.V.

  The following presented written comments in support of Sunset Property Services: Daniel
  W. James, M.V.; Wendy Bucknum, M.V.; Dennis O’Connor, M.V.; Michael Alarcon,
  M.V.; and James Leach; South Orange County Chamber of Commerce, Laguna Hills.

  Motion made by Mayor Leckness, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to direct staff to
  explore the option of changing the street sweeping from every other week to every 3 or 4
  weeks on certain residential streets and depending on the time of year.

  On roll call, said motion failed by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley and Leckness
  NOES:  Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  ABSENT:  None

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Council Member Schlicht, to (1)
  terminate the existing Fourth Amendment, two-month contract extension with Sunset
  Property Services as of July 31, 2011; (2) award a contract for the subject services to
  Arakelian Enterprise, Inc., dba Athens Services (A11-54) for the period of August 1, 2011,
  through June 30, 2013, in the amount of $653,868.00 (3) authorize staff to issue a purchase
City Council Minutes  8  July 5, 2011
   order to Arakelian Enterprises, Inc., dba Athens Services for the period of August 1, 2011
  through June 30, 2012 in an amount not to exceed $316,934.00 pending adoption of the
  Fiscal Year 2011-2013 budget by the City Council.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

RECESS

At the hour of 9:53 p.m., Mayor Leckness declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at
10:03 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

NEW BUSINESS

23. Second Amendment to Owner Participation Agreement, including First Amendment
  to Covenants Agreement and Maintenance Agreement, between or among the
  Community Development Agency of the City of Mission Viejo ("CDA" or "Agency"),
  and/or the City of Mission Viejo as the Successor Agency of the CDA, and Crown
  Valley Holdings LLC, a Delaware limited liability company ("Developer" or
  "Owner")

  Special Counsel Celeste Brady presented the staff report and answered questions of the
  City Council.

  Larry Gilbert, M.V.: expressed concern with the proposed project and stated that the
  Council should adopt a non-binding resolution.

  Colby Durnin, M.V.: provided clarification on the proposed LA Fitness project and the plan
  to re-energize Kaleidoscope center.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to
  adopt Resolution No. 11-44 Approving the Second Amendment to Owner Participation
  Agreement, with attachments thereto that include First Amendment to Covenants
  Agreement and Maintenance Agreement.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

City Council Minutes  9  July 5, 2011
 4.  State Legislative Advocacy and Government Relations Services

  Heather Dion Stratman, Senior Director, Townsend Public Affairs Irvine: answered
  Council Member Reardon’s questions and outlined her firm’s legislative support services.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, to approve the
  proposed Professional Services Agreement with Townsend Public Affairs for State
  legislative advocacy and government relations services for a total not to exceed amount of
  $60,000 for the period of July 6, 2011, to June 30, 2012.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

*Items 6 and 14 were considered together.

6.  2011 Residential Resurfacing (CIP 838)

  Council Members Reardon and Schlicht expressed concern about the contractor, All
  American Asphalt, due to problems on Olympiad Road.

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon described that the issues on Olympiad Road had
  nothing to do with contractor performance but rather it was an issue with the materials. He
  noted that All American Asphalt guaranteed their work and removed the deficient slurry
  seal and staff is comfortable awarding a new contract to the company.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to award
  the construction contract for the subject project to All American Asphalt in the amount of
  $5,052,540.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

8.  Acceptable Condition Levels for the City’s Street Network

  Council Member Schlicht expressed concern with the new pavement rating system.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to
  establish the range of acceptable average condition levels for all classifications of road
  types within the City’s street network at either "Good" or "Very Good," as defined by the
  Pavement Condition Index (PCI), for fiscal years 2011-12 and 2012-13.
City Council Minutes  10  July 5, 2011
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Leckness, to adopt
  acceptable condition levels for all three classifications and road types, within the City’s
  street network, of either very good or good as defined by the Pavement Condition Index.

  Mayor Leckness withdrew his second and the motion died for lack of a second.

Motion made by Mayor Leckness, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to continue the
meeting beyond the 11:00 p.m. hour.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

9.  City of Mission Viejo Seven-Year Public Works Capital Improvement Program
  (Fiscal Year 2011-2012 through Fiscal Year 2017-2018)

  Council Member Schlicht expressed concern with pedestrian crossing between the lake and
  the Youth Athletic Park and she asked why that is not included in this CIP program.

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon announced that the matter was studied by staff
  and the Traffic Committee and he would be happy to share the results of the report with
  Council Member Schlicht.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Leckness, to (1) adopt
  Resolution 11-42A Adopting a Seven-Year Public Works Capital Improvement Program
  beginning with the 2011-2012 Fiscal Year; and (2) direct the Director of Public Works to
  transmit the Seven-Year Public Works Capital Improvement Program to the Orange County
  Transportation Authority by August 15, 2011.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

11. Oso Parkway Widening, I-5 to Country Club Drive (CIP 791)-Acquisition of Right-of-
  Way

City Council Minutes  11  July 5, 2011
   Council Member Reardon commended Mark Chagnon for doing a good job on the Oso
  Parkway widening project.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, to (1) approve
  the Agreement for Acquisition of Real Property between the City of Mission Viejo and
  Mission Viejo Country Club in the amount of $946,815 for the purchase of the necessary
  right-of-way and landscape maintenance easements required for the widening of Oso
  Parkway from I-5 to Country Club Drive; (2) authorize the City Clerk to record the
  easement deeds in the office of the County Recorder subject to any minor revisions
  required by the City Attorney and City Engineer.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

13. Parking Restrictions on Bellogente South of Crown Valley

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, to continue
  Consent Calendar items 13 and 18 to the City Council Meeting of August 15, 2011.|

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

14. Avery Parkway Pavement Rehabilitation, Camino Capistrano to Marguerite Parkway

  This item was discussed during item number 6.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, to award the

City Council Minutes  12  July 5, 2011
   Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Mayor Leckness, to (1) adopt

  adopt Resolution 11-03 Authorizing investment in the State Local Agency Investment

  Council Member Reardon commended Director Chagnon for completing the project within

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, to approve

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

24. Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Council Member Kelley announced that she would defer her report to the next meeting.

25. Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Ury presented the report.
City Council Minutes  13  July 5, 2011
 26. San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Leckness announced that he had nothing to report.

27. Investment Advisory Commission Vacancy

  By consensus, the City Council directed the City Clerk to post and publish a notice of
  vacancy on the Investment Advisory Commission.

STAFF REPORTS (Continued)

City Attorney’s Report

32. City Council Determination Regarding a need for City Recreation Facility Use of and
  at O’Neill Elementary School and Direction to the City Manager to advise Saddleback
  Valley Unified School District of the City’s Interest in Exercising its Statutory Priority
  to Lease the Whole of the Subject Site

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to adopt
  Resolution 11-48 Determining that the City has a need for additional exterior and interior
  recreation space (4/5’s vote required); and further direct the City Manager to advise
  Saddleback Valley Unified School District of the City’s interest in exercising to lease the
  whole of the O’Neill School site pursuant to statute.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

33. Update Regarding Assembly Bill 1x26 and 1x27

  Special Counsel Celeste Brady provided an update on AB 1x26 and 1x27.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

34. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented
  in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Kelley

City Council Minutes  14  July 5, 2011
 Council Member Kelley complimented the Mission Viejo Activities Committee on an excellent
4th of July Street Faire. It was another outstanding event provided by a core of volunteers and
she recognized and thanked them for their hard work. She also attended the Swim Meet of
Champions on June 26 and she was able to see the new starting blocks that the City helped to
pay for. The equipment looks great and it was a wonderful event as always. Council Member
Kelley encouraged residents to attend the Pacific Symphony Prelude in the Park on July 30,
2011. She concluded her comments by announcing that the Community of Character word for
the month of July is fairness.

Council Member Reardon

Council Member Reardon echoed Council Member Kelley's comments on the 4th of July Street
Faire. She volunteered at the event and she noted it was wonderful day that ended with a great
fireworks show. She also announced that she attended the Capistrano Valley High School
graduation and she was especially inspired by a Significant Selected Scholar who is legally blind
and is heading to Berkley and hoping to become a doctor. Lastly Council Member Reardon
shared video of 4 year-old Cade who is making a miraculous recovery from brain cancer and a
subsequent stroke.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht outlined her attendance at recent meetings and the 4th of July Street
Fair. She noted that she misses the Rotary Club's root beer floats but it was a great day. She
announced that there will be a public hearing at the Planning Commission meeting on July 11
regarding the UDR apartment complex and she invited residents to attend and become
involved. She expressed her concerns with the budget and stated that the Council cannot
compromise City standards and values by maximizing the amount of money the City can get out
of a developer. Council Member Schlicht announced that the Council will be dark until August
15 and she concluded her comments with a quote from Ronald Reagan: "Let the Fourth of July
always be a reminder that here in this land, for the first time, it was decided that man is born with
certain God-given rights; that government is only a convenience created and managed by the
people, with no powers of its own except those voluntarily granted to it by the people. We
sometimes forget that great truth, and we never should."

Mayor Pro Tem Ury

Mayor Pro Tem Ury stated that it was an outstanding 4th of July Street Faire and fireworks show
and he wished everyone a great summer.
